name: Reflex

modes.label: Hosted Python apps
modes.note: Compute = machine type (CPU/RAM allocated per instance, e.g. 'c2m4') x number of regions x instance runtime; idle instances accrue nothing and wake on request; Persistent Machine 'Coming soon'. Per-machine-type prices are not published anywhere public (only via 'reflex cloud vmtypes' when logged in). Default region sjc.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 1 published app on Reflex Cloud, shared compute, limited AI generation + hosting usage that 'refills periodically' (amount not published), public apps/repos only, 1 workspace user, 7-day logs, no always-on (apps idle-sleep), no custom domains.

plans.name: Pro 25
plans.note: Pro variants $25/$50/$100/$200 give the same dollar amount as a monthly allowance shared by AI generation (AI Builder credits) and app hosting. No published overage: 'Choose a higher Pro monthly usage allowance for more capacity.' 1 workspace user; multiple apps; shared or dedicated compute; multi-region; always-on deployments; 90-day logs. Same note applies to Pro 50/100/200.

caveats: Free 1 published app with periodically refilled limited usage. Pro $25/$50/$100/$200 monthly allowance shared by AI generation and hosting. No session limits does not mean unlimited CPU-hours.

Shared/dedicated deployment sizes and regions offered but no per-vCPU/RAM list tariff on pricing page. Enterprise on own Google Cloud, SSO, on-prem and air-gap options quote. Open-source Apache-2.0 framework is not free managed infrastructure.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Seats: 'Each organization member uses a seat. A pending invitation also holds a seat'. Seat price is not published; Free and Pro allow 1 workspace user, more users/team workspaces are Enterprise (contact sales).

BYOC (Enterprise only) deploys to your own AWS ECS, Google Cloud Run or Azure Container Apps via 'reflex cloud deploy --aws/--gcp/--azure'; managed Google Cloud connection also Enterprise. Self-host on-prem/air-gapped is Enterprise.

fleet.tiers: Free includes 1 hosted app on shared compute; Pro provides higher hosting usage; enterprise app limits customized.
fleet.notes: One hosted app is not necessarily one VM: deployment can use multiple regions and managed instance lifecycle. No aggregate new-account instance/vCPU/GPU quota established; persistent machines not yet available per compute docs.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The deployment form may show a disabled Persistent Machine option. This feature is not available yet. When disabled, Reflex manages app instances and can scale them down when idle.
snapshot_auto.note: Managed stateless app instances; idle instances scale down and wake on request with no state saved ('include_db' local SQLite 'is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts'). AI Builder auto-creates source-code checkpoints per agent message (restore-checkpoint) - app source only, not machine state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A rollback redeploys a previous deployment's stored image and makes it current without rebuilding from source
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine/disk snapshot API. Only deployment-image history/rollback, Builder source checkpoints, and Fork/Copy app (copies source files).

secret_proxy.quote: Apps receive the values as environment variables at runtime.
secret_proxy.note: Project/app secrets and integration credentials become env vars read via os.environ; 'Sensitive' mode hides values from team members only. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: This database is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts. Use a database service for production data.
volume_attach.note: No volumes in cloud.yml or docs; 'Persistent Machine' is marked 'Coming soon' on machine-types page. Use external DB/storage integrations.

volume_shared.quote: Include local sqlite database: include_db: true This database is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts. Use a database service for production data.
volume_shared.note: Reflex Cloud's config-file and compute docs document no volume resource at all (only ephemeral local SQLite via include_db, explicitly non-persistent, and env-var secrets). The Machine Types/compute page confirms the only disk-like feature, 'Persistent Machine', is 'not available yet' (https://reflex.dev/docs/hosting/compute/). With no persistent volume feature offered at all, a shared-volume-across-machines feature cannot exist; volume_shared=false is confirmed rather than an unbacked 'no'.

isolation.quote: vmtype string c1m1 Virtual machine specifications
isolation.note: Reflex Cloud describes app instances by 'vmtype' (e.g. c1m1) and runs deployments in Kubernetes namespaces on self-hosted/on-prem installs ('A project's Kubernetes namespace decides which cluster tenant its sandboxes run in'). This is a managed-app-instance PaaS, not a VM/microVM product with root/SSH; treated as shared-kernel container isolation despite the 'virtual machine specifications' marketing label.

image_oci.quote: packages array empty Additional system packages ... Package names are based on the apt package manager
image_oci.note: Deployment config lets you add apt packages to Reflex's own build image; there is no documented option to start from a custom Docker/OCI image on Reflex Cloud. Self-hosting via Docker builds Reflex's own container, not user-supplied images.

docker_inside.quote: Reflex Cloud measures compute while an app instance is running.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Reflex Cloud is a managed Python-app hosting PaaS (build/deploy a Reflex app); no documented ability to run Docker/containers inside the hosted app instance.

nested_virt.quote: Reflex Cloud measures compute while an app instance is running.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no /dev/kvm or VM-inside-VM capability is documented for hosted app instances.

desktop.quote: Reflex is the open-source Python framework for building full-stack web apps in pure Python.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

browser.quote: Reflex is the open-source Python framework for building full-stack web apps in pure Python.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the AI Builder itself uses screenshots/preview iframes of the built app, not a managed browser/browser-automation product for users.

computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.quote: List all the regions of the hosting service.
egress_ip_type.note: Hosted apps run on Reflex's cloud infrastructure across named datacenter regions (e.g. fra, iad); no residential/mobile egress product is documented.

ssh.quote: Connect through an SSH Tunnel ... Use an SSH tunnel when the database is on a private network but can be reached through a bastion host.
ssh.note: SSH only appears as a client-side tunnel to reach an external database from Reflex Build; no documented SSH access into the hosted app instance itself. Logs/CLI provide 'terminal-based inspection' of logs, not a shell.

snapshot.quote: The deployment form may show a disabled Persistent Machine option. This feature is not available yet. When disabled, Reflex manages app instances and can scale them down when idle.
snapshot.note: No disk/filesystem or memory machine snapshot exists. The only state-like features are: (1) deployment 'History and Rollback' which 'redeploys a previous deployment's stored image ... without rebuilding from source' (reflex.dev/docs/hosting/app-management/) - that is a container-image/source rollback, not a running machine's disk/memory snapshot; and (2) AI Builder auto-checkpoints of source code per agent message - also source, not machine state. include_db local SQLite is explicitly 'not persistent and is lost when the app restarts' (reflex.dev/docs/hosting/config-file/). No fork-a-running-machine feature exists either (the 'Fork/Copy app' action just copies source files). So there is no contradiction: snapshot=none is confirmed, not merely unbacked.

fork.quote: A rollback redeploys a previous deployment's stored image and makes it current without rebuilding from source
fork.note: Reflex Build offers a 'Fork/Copy app' feature that copies an app's source files into a new app; this is a source-level fork, not a running-machine clone.

fork_running.quote: The deployment form may show a disabled Persistent Machine option. This feature is not available yet.
fork_running.note: No running-machine clone capability; app instances are stateless and managed by Reflex, and persistent machines are not yet available.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The deployment form may show a disabled Persistent Machine option. This feature is not available yet.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-including clone/fork feature is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Idle instances do not accrue compute usage and wake when the app receives another request.
pause_resume.note: Idle instances scale to zero and wake on request automatically (auto_stop_idle/wake_on_request), but there is no explicit user-invoked pause/resume API for a machine.

persistent_disk.quote: This database is not persistent and is lost when the app restarts. Use a database service for production data.
persistent_disk.note: Local SQLite/instance storage is not persistent across restarts; no documented persistent disk for app instances.

live_resize.quote: --vmtype TEXT: The virtual machine type to scale to.
live_resize.note: Changing vmtype ('scale to') is exposed as a redeploy/scale operation via the CLI, with no documentation that it resizes a running instance in place without recreating it; treated as not live resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: The page provides client-specific instructions for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and Windsurf.
agent_harnesses.note: Reflex ships an MCP server and agent-skills so external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) can use Reflex docs while building Reflex apps locally; it does not preinstall/offer these harnesses running inside a Reflex Cloud sandbox/app instance.

harness_api.quote: The Reflex MCP server provides structured access to Reflex docs and component information
harness_api.note: Reflex's MCP server exposes documentation/component context to external coding tools, not an API that drives a coding harness running inside a Reflex-hosted machine.

own_agent_api.quote: Reflex is the open-source Python framework for building full-stack web apps in pure Python.
own_agent_api.note: Reflex Build's AI app-generation agent is driven through its own chat UI (Builder), not exposed as a first-party API for driving a browser/computer-use/research task agent.

lang_node.quote: The REFLEX_DIR environment variable can be set, which allows users to set the location where Reflex writes helper tools like Bun and NodeJS.
lang_node.note: Reflex's own build toolchain provisions and uses Node.js/Bun to build the frontend, so a Node runtime is present in the build/runtime environment.

public_ipv4.note: Apps are reached via managed subdomains/custom domains over HTTPS; no documented dedicated public IPv4 address per app instance.

ingress_rules.note: No documented IP allowlisting, private/auth URL, or security-group style ingress control for hosted apps beyond custom domain/hostname assignment.

egress_allowlist.quote: Reflex Cloud measures compute while an app instance is running.
egress_allowlist.note: No documented outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode for Reflex Cloud app instances.

egress_http_rules.quote: Reflex Cloud measures compute while an app instance is running.
egress_http_rules.note: No documented HTTP method/path-level egress rules for app instances.

guest_firewall.quote: vmtype string c1m1 Virtual machine specifications
guest_firewall.note: Not a full VM/microVM with root/SSH access (root/ssh both false here), so the 'derived' guest-firewall assumption for full-VM products does not apply; no nftables/iptables control is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: List all the regions of the hosting service.
static_egress_ip.note: No documented fixed/static outbound IP for hosted app instances.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — vmtypes (e.g. c1m1) are CPU/RAM machine sizes for hosting Python web apps; no GPU machine type is documented.

windows.quote: List all the regions of the hosting service.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Reflex Cloud hosts Python web apps on Linux instances; no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: List all the regions of the hosting service.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machine option is documented for Reflex Cloud hosting.

eu_data_residency.note: Reflex Cloud lets a deployment choose region mappings including EU regions (e.g. 'fra' Frankfurt), so app compute can be kept in the EU; broader org-level 'EU data residency' guarantee for all data is not separately documented.

max_session_h.quote: Idle instances do not accrue compute usage and wake when the app receives another request.
max_session_h.note: No documented maximum runtime/session cutoff for a running app instance; instances run until idled or redeployed, so treated as no hard session cap (billing/behavior differs from a sandbox time limit).

arm64.quote: Machine types define the CPU and RAM allocated to each app instance.
arm64.note: Machine types (e.g. 'c2m4') are defined only by CPU/RAM allocation; no architecture/ARM option is documented anywhere in compute, machine-types, or BYOC (GCP/AWS/Azure) docs. Reflex Cloud is a managed PaaS with no customer-selectable CPU architecture, so ARM64 is not offered: outside the product's scope.
